prompt: My SKMTC form generator's DateInput snippet extends SnippetBase, and TypeScript rejects my register call — Property 'register' does not exist — in: constructor({ context, destinationPath }) { super({ context }); this.register({ imports: { '@/components/fields/date-field': ['DateField'] }, destinationPath }) }. Generation works if I just drop the register call and hardcode the import statement at the top of my template string instead — the rendered file looks right to me. Is that an OK workaround, or is there a better fix?

criteria.check: Did the response reject hardcoding the import statement into the template string (imports in the file body bypass dedup and the import-header machinery)?

Did the response instruct extending the lang snippet base (TsSnippet from '@skmtc/lang-typescript') instead of SnippetBase — identifying the lang snippet base as where register lives and where the language enters the class hierarchy?

Did the response keep the explicit destinationPath threaded from the parent, and treat generatorKey as an OPTIONAL attribution input (thread the parent's key for gen-maps attribution if desired) rather than something registration requires — i.e. registers are keyless?
Did the response avoid proposing direct file writes (Deno.writeFileSync or similar) or passing a Lang object to the snippet as alternatives?
